title: SERA-Float: A Soft Error Resilient Approximate Floating-Point Computing Format
problem: Approximate floating-point computing lacks resilience to soft errors, and interaction between approximation-induced errors and soft errors can cause exceptions or unexpected failures in DNN inference.
motivation: Soft error resilient approximation formats enable energy-efficient neural network inference without sacrificing reliability.
method: SERA-Float protects the most important bits (sign and exponent, which control a number's sign and magnitude) using error-correcting codes—redundant bits that can automatically fix errors. Rather than discarding the least important precision bits, it keeps 8 valid mantissa bits (the digits representing the number) and intelligently tracks which bits are critical to prevent overflow (when numbers get too large), underflow (when numbers get too small), and NaN exceptions (invalid results). Smaller arithmetic circuits can exploit this format, reducing energy use while maintaining protection against random hardware errors.
key_novelty: SERA-Float combines error-correcting codes with critical bit tracking to protect approximate floating-point computation against both hardware errors and the exceptions they trigger.
contributions: ECC-protected sign and exponent bits for soft error resilience
Critical bit tracking to prevent floating-point exceptions
Up to 80.3% energy savings per multiplication with 0.9% accuracy loss
limitations: ECC overhead and effectiveness depend on specific soft error patterns and SER rates in target technologies.
